title: Israel Oppressed in Egypt
summary: Jacob's descendants multiply in Egypt until a new king who did not know Joseph fears their numbers and sets taskmasters over them to build store cities. The harder they are worked, the more they grow. Pharaoh orders the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah, to kill newborn boys; they fear God and refuse, and God blesses them. Pharaoh then commands all his people to throw every Hebrew boy into the river.

title: The Birth and Rescue of Moses
summary: A Levite woman hides her newborn son for three months, then places him in a basket of reeds sealed with pitch among the flags at the river's edge while his sister watches. Pharaoh's daughter, bathing there, finds him and takes pity though she knows he is a Hebrew child. His sister offers to find a nurse and fetches his own mother, who is paid to nurse him. He grows up as the princess's son and is named Moses.

title: Moses Flees to Midian
summary: Grown, Moses sees an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, kills him and hides the body. The next day a Hebrew asks whether he means to kill him too, and Moses, learning the deed is known, flees to Midian when Pharaoh seeks his life. At a well he drives off shepherds who harass the daughters of Reuel, the priest of Midian, marries Zipporah, and names their son Gershom. Meanwhile Israel groans in bondage, and God hears and remembers his covenant.

title: The Burning Bush
summary: Tending Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed and hears God call his name. God says he has seen Israel's affliction, gives his name as 'I AM THAT I AM', and sends Moses to bring the people out of Egypt. Moses objects that he is nobody, that the people will not believe him, and that he is slow of speech. God gives him signs of a staff turned serpent and a hand turned leprous, and appoints Aaron as his spokesman.

title: Moses Returns to Egypt
summary: Moses asks Jethro's leave and sets out for Egypt with his wife, sons and the staff of God. God tells him he will harden Pharaoh's heart and that Israel is his firstborn son. At a lodging place the LORD meets Moses and seeks to kill him until Zipporah circumcises her son; the text does not explain the episode. Aaron meets Moses at the mountain of God, and when the elders see the signs, the people believe and bow in worship.

title: Moses and Aaron Before Pharaoh
summary: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel hold a feast to the LORD in the wilderness, and Pharaoh answers, 'Who is the LORD?' He makes the work harder by making Israel gather their own straw while keeping the brick quota. The foremen are beaten and blame Moses, who complains to God. God answers that he will bring Israel out and renews his promise to the patriarchs, but the people will not listen, for anguish of spirit and cruel bondage.

title: The Plagues of Egypt
summary: Moses and Aaron confront Pharaoh through nine plagues: the Nile turns to blood, then come frogs, gnats, flies, disease on livestock, boils, hail, locusts and darkness. Egypt's magicians match the first signs, then fail, and Goshen is spared from several. Pharaoh repeatedly relents and bargains over who may go, then reverses himself. The text says both that Pharaoh hardened his heart and that the LORD hardened it.

title: The Passover and the Death of the Firstborn
summary: God tells Moses that one last plague will kill every firstborn in Egypt. Israel is told to keep the Passover: each household takes a lamb, marks its doorposts with the blood, and eats it roasted with unleavened bread and bitter herbs, dressed to leave. At midnight the LORD strikes the firstborn of Egypt, from Pharaoh's son to the prisoner's, and passes over the marked houses. Pharaoh urges Israel to go, and Egyptians give them silver, gold and clothing.

title: The Exodus from Egypt
summary: About 600,000 men on foot, with children, livestock and a mixed multitude, leave Rameses for Succoth after 430 years in Egypt. Rules are given for Passover and unleavened bread, and the firstborn of people and animals are consecrated to the LORD. Moses takes the bones of Joseph, as Joseph had asked. God leads them by the wilderness road rather than through Philistine country, in a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.

title: Crossing the Sea
summary: Pharaoh changes his mind and pursues Israel, trapping them at the sea, and the people cry out against Moses. Moses tells them to stand still. The angel of God and the pillar of cloud move between the camps, and a strong east wind divides the sea so Israel crosses on dry ground. When the Egyptians follow, the water returns and drowns them. Moses and Israel sing to the LORD, and Miriam leads the women with timbrels.

title: Bitter Water, Manna and Quail
summary: After three days without water Israel finds bitter water at Marah, which Moses makes sweet by throwing in a tree. In the wilderness of Sin the people say they would have been better off in Egypt, and God promises bread. Quail come in the evening and manna in the morning, gathered by the omer; what is kept overnight spoils, except on the sixth day, when a double portion is gathered for the Sabbath. An omer of manna is kept before the testimony.

title: Water from the Rock and the Battle with Amalek
summary: At Rephidim there is no water, and the people quarrel with Moses and test the LORD. God tells Moses to strike the rock at Horeb before the elders, and water comes out; the place is called Massah and Meribah. Amalek then attacks. While Joshua fights, Moses stands on the hill with the staff, and Israel prevails when his hands are up. Aaron and Hur support his hands, and the LORD vows war against Amalek from generation to generation.

title: Jethro Advises Moses
summary: Moses' father-in-law Jethro brings Moses' wife Zipporah and two sons to the camp at the mountain of God. Moses tells him of the exodus, and Jethro rejoices, blesses the LORD, and offers sacrifice with Aaron and the elders. Next day he sees Moses judging the people from morning to evening and warns him it is too heavy. He advises teaching the law and appointing capable men over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens, then returns home.

title: The Covenant and Ten Commandments at Sinai
summary: In the third month Israel camps before Sinai, and God tells them through Moses that they will be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation if they keep his covenant. The people consecrate themselves for three days, and the mountain is fenced off. The LORD descends in thunder, lightning, smoke and fire and speaks the Ten Commandments. The people tremble and ask Moses to speak with them instead, and he draws near the thick darkness where God is.

title: The Covenant Is Sealed at Sinai
summary: Moses writes the LORD's words and builds an altar with twelve pillars. Young men offer burnt and peace offerings, and Moses reads the book of the covenant; the people answer, 'All that the LORD hath said will we do.' He sprinkles blood on the altar and on the people. Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu and seventy elders go up and see the God of Israel and eat and drink; then Moses and Joshua ascend, and Moses enters the cloud for forty days and nights.

title: The Golden Calf
summary: While Moses is on the mountain, the people ask Aaron for gods. Aaron collects their gold earrings, fashions a golden calf, and proclaims a feast to the LORD. God tells Moses, who pleads for the people, then sees the calf and the dancing and breaks the tablets. He burns the calf, grinds it, and makes Israel drink it. The Levites rally to him and about three thousand die; Aaron blames the people, and Moses offers to be blotted out of God's book with them.

title: Moses Sees God's Glory
summary: The LORD tells Moses to go on to the land but says he will not go among a stiff-necked people. Moses pitches the tent of meeting outside the camp, and the LORD speaks with him face to face. Moses asks to see his glory and is hidden in a cleft of the rock while the LORD passes proclaiming his name, merciful and gracious. New tablets are cut and the covenant is renewed, and Moses' face shines so that he veils it before the people.

title: Building the Tabernacle
summary: Moses assembles Israel, repeats the Sabbath law, and the people bring so many gifts that they are told to stop. Bezaleel and Aholiab, filled with God's spirit, direct the skilled workers who make the tabernacle, ark, table, lampstand, altars and priestly garments. Moses inspects and blesses the finished work. On the first day of the first month of the second year the tabernacle is set up, and the cloud covers the tent as the glory of the LORD fills it.
